answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying reputation to verifiable, costly work rather than to free account creation: each identity must earn trust through a history of completed jobs that peers can audit, like tending a garden where only sustained care yields fruit. A sudden gale of new accounts therefore cannot flood the market, because newcomers start with no audited record and must prove reliability slowly, while a shared lagoon of attestations lets honest agents check each other's past before delegating valuable work.
